page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server contains 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-level features such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block reads and writes, but small-block cached reads are relatively weak. Cryptographic capabilities are average, as shown by the Passmark CPU encryption test, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are positioned in the lower 25% tier.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the n2d-standard-4 offers a predictable hardware profile for entry-level general-purpose workloads. Its strong single-core performance makes it suitable for applications that cannot easily parallelize, such as lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving. However, the weak multi-core scaling and lower database performance suggest it is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded processing, large-scale databases, or complex compilation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose server configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% in stress-ng tests, though multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations generally fall into the lower 25% tier. Large-block memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression tasks perform at an average level. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads requiring dedicated resources but limited multi-threaded scaling, such as basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications.
